source_title: Article 7: Central Retail District (C-R) - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.2.702)
quote: L(17) | Accessory structures are permitted subject to Sec. 10-2.2.703. Property Development Regulations.

finding: C-R has no minimum front, side, corner-side or rear setback (NA), but D(11) points to the General Plan building-setback figure, and the creek setback may still apply.
source_title: Article 7: Central Retail District (C-R) - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.2.703)
quote:

finding: Walnut Creek bans outdoor storage in every zone except a short list of uses, and general retail inventory storage is not on that list.
value: Outdoor storage prohibited except listed uses (WCMC 10-2.3.121.B)
source_title: Article 1: Site Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.3.121)
quote: Outdoor sales, service, display of merchandise or products, and storage shall be prohibited in any zone district except as follows:

finding: The stated intent is to allow outdoor storage only where there is no feasible alternative, and the stricter provision controls when sections conflict.
source_title: Article 1: Site Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.3.121)
quote: The intent of this section is to limit outdoor sales, service, display and storage to those uses or situations where there is no feasible alternative.

finding: The only outdoor-structure exception (pumps, tanks, pipes) requires a health/safety need or infeasibility of indoor placement plus Design Review Commission approval, so it is not a clear fit for inventory containers.
source_title: Article 1: Site Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.3.121.B.10)
quote: Accessory structures such as pumps, tanks, pipes when it can be demonstrated that an outdoor location is needed for health and safety consideration or when, due to structure size, it is not feasible to locate the structure within a building and Design Review Commission approval has been granted.

finding: In C-R, Retail Sales/Rental is allowed only if all activity is inside an enclosed building; outdoor sales need a Conditional Use Permit.
source_title: Article 7: Central Retail District (C-R) - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.2.702)
quote: Permitted provided that all activity is conducted entirely within an enclosed building. Uses that include outdoor sales are permitted upon approval of a Conditional Use Permit subject to a finding that the outdoor sales does not negatively impact any abutting uses.

finding: The C-R use table gives no P, L or U for Mini-Storage or for Wholesaling, Distribution and Storage, so stand-alone storage uses appear not to be permitted in C-R.
value: Mini-Storage / Wholesaling, Distribution and Storage: blank (not listed)
source_title: Article 7: Central Retail District (C-R) - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.2.702)
quote: | 17. Mini-Storage |  |  |

finding: Temporary Activity Permits cover short promotional events (5 days or less) and listed seasonal activities, none of which is storage containers; applications need four scaled site plans at least 10 days ahead, routed to the Fire District.
value: Short-term ≤5 consecutive days; Seasonal ≥16 days; submit 10 days prior
source_title: Article 1: Site Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.3.118)
quote: Four dimensioned and scaled site plans shall be submitted to the Community Development Director for review of zoning compliance a minimum of ten (10) days prior to the commencement of any activity. The site plans shall be referred to the Consolidated Fire District

finding: Non-residential lot areas used to store equipment or materials must be paved and kept orderly.
source_title: Article 1: Site Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.3.116)
quote: lot areas not covered by buildings, but which are used for any nonresidential or nonagricultural purpose including, but not limited to, the repair or storage of vehicles, equipment and materials, shall be paved and maintained in an orderly manner at all times.

finding: Placing a container (a structure) needs design review; a new structure of 500 sf or less is a minor project.
source_title: Article 12: Design Review - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 10-2.4.12xx)
quote: The construction of a new structure of five hundred (500) square feet or less in size.

finding: Unverified: I found no Walnut Creek provision that names cargo, shipping or portable storage containers; ask the Duty Planner whether a 20/40-ft container in C-R is an accessory structure (design review plus building permit) or barred outdoor storage under 10-2.3.121, and whether any temporary allowance exists.
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek (Planning contact)
quote: Have Questions? Talk to a Planner via email at DutyPlanner@walnut-creek.org, phone at (925) 256-3558, or make an in-person appointment.

finding: Under the CBC, constructing, altering or moving any building or structure needs a building permit first.
source_title: Chapter 1 Scope and Administration - 2022 California Building Code (ICC)
quote: Any owner or owner’s authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure, or to erect, install, enlarge, alter, repair, remove, convert or replace any electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing system

finding: The CBC permit exemption covers only one-story detached storage sheds up to 120 sf; a 20-ft (about 160 sf) or 40-ft (about 320 sf) container is larger than that.
source_title: Chapter 1 Scope and Administration - 2022 California Building Code (ICC)
quote: One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided that the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet (11.15 m2).

finding: Temporary structure permits are time-limited and capped at 180 days unless the building official grants an extension.
source_title: Chapter 1 Scope and Administration - 2022 California Building Code (ICC)
quote: The building official is authorized to issue a permit for temporary structures and temporary uses. Such permits shall be limited as to time of service, but shall not be permitted for more than 180 days.

finding: Permit applications need a scaled site plan showing distances from lot lines and any flood hazard areas, which matters for the rear-of-lot creek setback.
source_title: Chapter 1 Scope and Administration - 2022 California Building Code (ICC)
quote: accompanied by a site plan showing to scale the size and location of new construction and existing structures on the site, distances from lot lines, the established street grades and the proposed finished grades and, as applicable, flood hazard areas, floodways, and design flood elevations

finding: Walnut Creek adopted the 2025 CBC and replaced CBC Chapter 1 Division II (permits and exemptions) with its own Title 9 Chapter 0.5, so the local text governs exemptions.
source_title: CHAPTER 9-1: Building Code - City of Walnut Creek, CA (WCMC 9-1.01)
quote: Division II of Chapter 1 of the California Building Code is hereby deleted and replaced by Chapter 0.5 of this title.

finding: The City's own guidance: accessory structures of 120 sf or less need no permit, and anything over 120 sf needs a building permit.
source_title: Accessory Structures in Residential areas | City of Walnut Creek
quote: You do not need a permit for your accessory structure if it is 120 square feet or less. You will need to get building permits if you are doing any plumbing, electrical, or mechanical work.

finding: The City notes that work exempt from a building permit may still need a Use Permit.
source_title: Building Permit FAQs | City of Walnut Creek
quote: In some cases, while a building permit is not required, a Use Permit might be.

finding: For commercial alterations, design review must be done before the building permit application, and plans must be stamped by a California architect or engineer unless the work has no life-safety element.
source_title: Submittal Requirements for Commercial Alterations (Not Including Additions), Information Bulletin IB-012
quote: Design Review is required for all exterior remodeling of commercial buildings. Contact the Planning Division for Design Review information. Design Review is required by the municipal code and is required to be completed prior to submitting an application for building permit.

finding: Unverified: I could not read WCMC Title 9 Chapter 0.5 (the local permit-exemption list) or whether it treats shipping containers specially; ask Building (925-943-5834) whether a container on a commercial lot needs a permit, a foundation or anchorage, and an engineered submittal.
source_title: Building Permit FAQs | City of Walnut Creek
quote: You can check with staff if your work does not need a permit by calling 925-943-5834 or emailing BuildingTech@walnut-creek.org.

finding: Retail Sales/Rental needs 1 parking space per 250 sf of Rentable Floor Area (RFA).
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (Table A)
quote: | 25. Retail Sales/Rental | 1 per 250 sq. ft. of RFA |  | Group I |

finding: Existing parking cannot be reduced below the required number, and existing deficient parking cannot be reduced further, so containers cannot take required stalls.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: Retention of Existing Parking. When space actually being used for off-street parking in connection with any building or use provides less parking than the required parking, it shall not be further reduced in area or capacity

finding: Required parking must be on the same parcel, and any reduction or off-site parking needs a conditional/minor use permit under Sec. 10-2.3.203, which bears on the 3 off-site spaces.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: A reduction in the required number of parking spaces or the provision of off-site parking shall not be permitted unless a conditional use permit is issued pursuant to Sec.10-2.3.203.

finding: A Zoning Administrator minor use permit can reduce, share or move parking off-site, but the reduction is capped at 20% of required spaces and needs clear and convincing evidence of lower demand.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (10-2.3.203)
quote: The maximum reduction in the required number of spaces shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of the total number of spaces required for each use.

finding: Added parking is triggered by a major alteration: a change of use, expansion of use or addition that raises required parking by 10% or more.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: "Major alteration or use change" shall mean, for these parking requirements, a change of use, expansion of use or a building addition all of which would increase the required number of parking spaces by ten percent (10%) or more.

finding: Substantially altering a parking layout or its dimensions, such as removing stalls for containers, needs design review approval.
source_title: Article 12: Design Review - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: or substantially alter any parking layout or dimensions, or obtain any building or site development permit for such activities, without first obtaining design review approval

finding: A standard 90-degree stall is 8.5 ft x 18 ft with a 25-ft aisle, and every space must be enterable without other cars moving, which limits where containers can go.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (Parking Area Design Standards)

finding: Group I uses (including retail) under 10,000 sf need no loading space.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA (Table B)
quote: | Less than 10,000 sq. ft. | 0 |  |  |

finding: Unverified: the site's approved required-parking count, and whether the 3 off-site spaces rest on a recorded agreement or use permit, are unknown; ask Planning for the approved parking figure before giving up any stall.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: Off-street parking and loading spaces shall be provided in accordance with Section 10-2.3.206, Off-Street Parking and Loading Spaces Required, and shall be located on the same parcel as the structure or use, except as provided in Section 10-2.3.203.

finding: A Pleasant Hill response to CCCFCD comments states the County requires at least a 30-ft setback from the top of bank of unimproved earth channels.
value: 30 ft from top of bank (unimproved earth channels)
source_title: Responses to Contra Costa County Flood Control and Water Conservation District comments (Pleasant Hill PC 10-27-09, Attachment G)
quote: The County requires a minimum of 30-feet setback distance from the top of bank of unimproved earth channels.

finding: The same document says the County's setback studies called for a 2.5:1 slope for bank stability, which is the basis of a projected-slope setback line.
source_title: Responses to Contra Costa County Flood Control and Water Conservation District comments (Pleasant Hill PC 10-27-09, Attachment G)
quote: Studies performed by the County to produce their ordinance indicated a need to provide a 2.5:1 slope to ensure stability.

finding: A Contra Costa County EIR shows the Creek Structure Setback Line defaults to 30 ft and can be reduced only through a formal exception (unincorporated example).
source_title: 3.0 Project Description (Contra Costa County Draft EIR)
quote: Exception to the Creek Structure Setback Line, reducing setback from 30 to 20 feet (Lots 21 and 22) and establishing setback line at the top of the creek bank in consideration of topography (Lots 23 and 24)

finding: Work inside Flood Control District right-of-way needs an FC District Encroachment Permit; County drainage permits apply in unincorporated areas.
source_title: FAQs - Channels/Creeks/Waterways | Contra Costa County
quote: Within FC District right of ways (where FC District faculties were built and are maintained) a FC District Encroachment Permit is required.

finding: Walnut Creek Development Engineering requires a site development permit for drainage course alteration and acts as floodplain administrator for FEMA flood-zone projects.
source_title: Development Engineering | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Site development permit is required for grading, retaining walls over 3 feet in height, drainage course alteration, commercial parking lot and any landscaping as required by the Design Review Commission.

finding: Stormwater treatment is required only when a project creates or replaces 5,000 sf or more of impervious surface, so containers on existing pavement are unlikely to trigger it.
source_title: Development Engineering | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Stormwater treatment is required on new development projects that create or replace 5,000 square feet or more of impervious surface.

finding: The County drainage fee, collected by the City for CCCFCD, applies when development creates new impervious surface.
source_title: Building Permit and Developer Fee Summary, Information Bulletin IB-045
quote: County Drainage Fee Fee paid to the City or County for Required when development creates new impervious surfaces

finding: Unverified: I found no Walnut Creek code section adopting the CCCFCD 30-ft structure setback or a projected top-of-bank method for this parcel; ask Walnut Creek Engineering and CCCFCD for the setback line here and whether an unanchored container counts as a structure. County guidance says sheds closer than 10 ft to top of bank should be anchored.
source_title: Maintenance of Creeks on Private Property (El Cerrito; diagrams credited to Contra Costa County Public Works)
quote: Sheds or other small structures closer than 10 feet from the top of the bank should be anchored to the ground.

finding: Fire apparatus access roads need at least 20 ft of unobstructed width and 13 ft 6 in of vertical clearance.
source_title: Chapter 5 Fire Service Features - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: Fire apparatus access roads shall have an unobstructed width of not less than 20 feet (6096 mm), exclusive of shoulders, except for approved security gates in accordance with Section 503.6, and an unobstructed vertical clearance of not less than 13 feet 6 inches (4115 mm).

finding: Fire access roads may not be obstructed in any way, so containers cannot sit in a required fire lane.
source_title: Chapter 5 Fire Service Features - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: Fire apparatus access roads shall not be obstructed in any manner, including the parking of vehicles. The minimum widths and clearances established in Sections 503.2.1 and 503.2.2 shall be maintained at all times.

finding: An access road must reach within 150 ft of all parts of the facility and the building's first-story exterior walls.
source_title: Chapter 5 Fire Service Features - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: The fire apparatus access road shall comply with the requirements of this section and shall extend to within 150 feet (45 720 mm) of all portions of the facility and all portions of the exterior walls of the first story of the building

finding: Outside combustible storage must be at least 10 ft from a lot line, or 3 ft if no higher than 6 ft, unless the fire code official approves less.
value: 10 ft from lot line (3 ft if ≤6 ft high)
source_title: Chapter 3 General Requirements - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: Outside storage of combustible materials shall not be located within 10 feet (3048 mm) of a lot line.

finding: In sprinklered buildings, combustible storage or display under eaves, canopies or overhangs is banned unless sprinklers are added there, which bears on the roofed walkway.
source_title: Chapter 3 General Requirements - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: Where buildings are protected by an automatic sprinkler system, the outdoor storage, display and handling of combustible materials under eaves, canopies or other projections or overhangs are prohibited except where automatic sprinklers are installed

finding: Indoor storage must stay 2 ft below the ceiling in non-sprinklered areas or 18 in below sprinkler deflectors, and may not be kept in exits.
source_title: Chapter 3 General Requirements - 2022 California Fire Code (ICC)
quote: Storage shall be maintained 2 feet (610 mm) or more below the ceiling in nonsprinklered areas of buildings or not less than 18 inches (457 mm) below sprinkler head deflectors in sprinklered areas of buildings.

finding: Commercial projects in Walnut Creek go to Contra Costa County Fire Protection District for review.
source_title: Outside Agencies and Districts | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Contra Costa County Fire Protection District Needed for: Commercial and Multi-Family Projects cccfpd.org (925) 930-5500

finding: Unverified: the CFC has no fixed container-to-building separation, and Walnut Creek now uses the 2025 codes, so section numbers may differ from the 2022 text quoted; ask CCCFPD for any required container separation, rug storage limits and access-route approval, and confirm 2025 CFC section numbers.
source_title: Construction and Permitting | Contra Costa County FPD
quote: Submittals must include two complete sets of scaled plans with each permit application. Plans should clearly show the scope of work and demonstrate compliance with the Fire Code and all applicable laws, ordinances, and regulations.

finding: No one may build or alter the exterior of any building or structure, or get a building permit for it, without design review approval first; enclosing the walkway with glazing is an exterior alteration.
source_title: Article 12: Design Review - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: No person shall erect, construct or alter the exterior of any building, structure or sign, or substantially alter any landscaping or other features required pursuant to any City approval

finding: Non-residential additions of 500 sf or less count as minor projects; the storefront's roughly 361 sf (195 + 166) would likely qualify.
source_title: Article 12: Design Review - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: Additions of five hundred (500) square feet or less in size to an existing multifamily or nonresidential development.

finding: The Community Development Director decides design review for minor projects, unless another entitlement in the same application goes to a higher body.
source_title: Article 12: Design Review - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: The Community Development Director shall act upon applications for ministerial design review and any other design review for minor projects, except as outlined below.

finding: All non-residential projects get Discretionary Design Review, judged against the Non-Residential Design Review Standards + Guidelines.
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Any project that does not qualify for Ministerial or Objective Design Review, including any residential development projects requiring a legislative amendment or additions to an existing residential project, shall undergo Discretionary Design Review. All non-residential projects are subject to this category of design review.

finding: Rentable Floor Area (the parking basis) excludes breezeways and open porches, so enclosing the roofed walkway and adding a vestibule likely adds RFA (about 361 sf, roughly 1.4 spaces at 1 per 250 sf).
source_title: Broadway Plaza Parking Space Reduction - Attachment 1 Draft Resolution (quoting WCMC 10-2.1.303)
quote: RFA is defined as the total area on all floors as measured to the inside surfaces of interior walls, excluding crawl spaces, garages, carports, breezeways, attics without floors, and open porches, balconies, terraces

finding: School district developer fees apply only when more than 500 sf of new conditioned area is created; a non-conditioned vestibule and enclosed walkway would likely not trigger them.
source_title: Outside Agencies and Districts | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Mt. Diablo Unified School District Needed for: only if more than 500 s.f. of new conditioned area is created

finding: Unverified: ask Planning whether the enclosed walkway and vestibule count as RFA (an addition) for parking, and whether the added spaces, against the building's total required parking, cross the 10% major-alteration threshold.
source_title: Article 2: Off-Street Parking, Loading, and TDM Regulations - City of Walnut Creek, CA
quote: In the following Tables, RFA stands for Rentable Floor Area and GFA stands for Gross Floor Area. For definitions of these two terms see Part I, Article 3. Definitions.

finding: Design review, minor use permit and use permit applications are all billed at the planning hourly rate.
source_title: Master Fee Schedule FY2026 & FY2027 - Community Development Planning
quote: | Minor Use Permit: | Minor Use Permit | per hour | 231.12 | 240.36 |

finding: A Short Term Promotional/Temporary Activity Permit is a flat fee equal to one hour of staff time.
source_title: Master Fee Schedule FY2026 & FY2027 - Community Development Planning
quote: | Short Term Promotional/Temporary Activity Permit | flat fee (one hour of time) | 231.12 | 240.36 |

finding: The building plan review fee equals 100% of the building permit fee, which is set from the project valuation.
source_title: Master Fee Schedule FY2026 & FY2027 - Building Division
quote: A Building Plan Review Fee shall be 100 percent of the Building Permit Fee, as shown in the applicable fee resolu tion adopted by the City Council.

finding: Building plan review moves to hourly billing after the third review round.
source_title: Fees, rates, and deposits | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Hourly fees are charged after the 3rd round of building division plan review.

finding: For commercial alterations, first review takes up to 18 business days (Planning 15, Building 18) and rechecks up to 13; commercial additions take up to 23 and 18.
value: Comm. alterations: 18 BD first / 13 BD recheck
source_title: Plan Review Turnaround Times (In Business Days), Policy Bulletin PB-031

finding: Over-the-counter permits take 3 to 7 days, and the first plan review takes 8 to 28 business days depending on project type.
value: OTC 3–7 days; first review 8–28 business days
source_title: Turnaround times | City of Walnut Creek
quote: The first review can take anywhere from 8 to 28 business days, depending on the project type. Future reviews can also take several weeks.

finding: After a design review submittal, a Notice of Application Status comes within 30 days, and each outside agency gets two weeks to comment.
value: 30 days to status notice; 2 weeks outside agencies
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: After submittal, a planner will be assigned to your project. Within 30 days after the submittal, you will get a Notice of Application Status.

finding: Small staff-level design review projects may take only a few weeks, though discretionary review time is not guaranteed.
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: Only a few weeks may be required for small, staff delegated projects.

finding: Planning contact is the Duty Planner by phone or email, and planning applications go through the City's online ACA permit portal.
source_title: Design Review | City of Walnut Creek
quote: All applications must be submitted via the City's Online Permit Portal, ACA Portal. First-time users will need to create a new account prior to submittal.

finding: Building permits are online-only (no paper or email applications); the Building Division is at 925-943-5834 or BuildingTech@walnut-creek.org.
source_title: Building Permits | City of Walnut Creek
quote: The City of Walnut Creek has fully committed to an all-online permitting system – all permit types shall be applied for via our Online Permit Portal. We are no longer accepting paper or emailed permit applications.

finding: A Commercial Express Review option lets the architect and MEP designers review plans with City staff in a virtual meeting, with recheck appointments on Mondays.
source_title: Commercial Express Review | City of Walnut Creek
